text:
sam: Heads-up — Canary for fp8-enabled serving on redwood-xt-3b showed a ~12% p99 per-token latency regression vs our int8 baseline. Not huge but reproducible across 3 runs.

maya: @sam can you paste the perf profile and the exact config you used for the canary?

sam: Repro steps: deploy canary route with quant_mode=fp8, kernel_policy=auto, batch_target=32, but traffic was synthetic seq=512 batch=4. Attached profiler dump below.

olga: dropping profiler dump. quick skim: lots of time in matmul kernel and memcpy. KV cache also has higher miss rate than expected.

profiler-bot: PERF PROFILE SUMMARY 
model: redwood-xt-3b 
quant: fp8 
kernel_policy: auto 
seq_len: 512 
batch: 4 
requests: 1200 
per_token_p50_ms: 0.7 
per_token_p95_ms: 1.7 
per_token_p99_ms: 2.8 
kernel_counters: {"matmul_fp8": 62, "matmul_int8": 0, "softmax_fp32": 9, "kv_lookup": 12, "memcpy": 10, "other": 7} 
kv_cache: hits=78%, misses=22% 
batching: avg_effective_batch=3.1 (target=4) 
notes: higher memcpy fraction vs int8 baseline (int8 memcpy=5%)

henri: Interesting — fp8 matmul is selected but memcpy went up. Could be alignment/packing overhead from fp8 kernels (repacking to 8-bit lanes). Also kv miss rate 22% is higher than usual for this workload — any prefix caching toggles?

sam: Prefix caching off for the canary (wanted simpler surface). When we re-ran with prefix_cache enabled, latency improved but still ~6% worse than int8 p99.

maya: Do we have per-token breakdown across generation steps? Does first token cost dominate or tail tokens?

olga: Here's a quick per-token trace (trimmed):
```
token_index, per_token_ms
0, 4.2
1, 1.1
2, 0.9
...
100, 0.8
200, 0.9
500, 1.2
```
Tail tokens slightly higher — maybe kernel switch when sequence length grows or KV concat cost.

profiler-bot: DETAILED KERNEL TRACE (excerpt) 
[matmul_fp8] calls=490, avg_ms=0.95,  p95=1.6 
[matmul_int8] calls=0 
[pack_to_fp8] calls=490, avg_ms=0.12 
[memcpy_host_device] calls=1340, avg_ms=0.07 
[kv_lookup] calls=630, avg_ms=0.18, hit_rate=0.78

sam: So pack_to_fp8 shows up as a new counter — that accounts for extra memcpy-ish cost. We don't account for pack time in kernel selection logic today.

henri: Two quick hypotheses: (1) pack overhead dominates for short sequences / small batches — makes fp8 win only at large effective batch or long matmuls; (2) calibration parameters (scale/zero) we used might cause fallback to slower kernels for certain layers — check kernel selection logs.

maya: We saw an earlier change in batching heuristics that reduces opportunistic batch coalescing for fp kernels to avoid OOMs. Could that explain avg_effective_batch=3.1 vs target 4?

olga: Yes. The new autoscaler lowers admission rate when memory margin is tight; with pack overhead memory spikes more often and admission gets conservative. Net effect: smaller batches -> worse perf.

sam: Proposal: instrument the serving metrics with these new counters: `kernel_choice`, `pack_overhead_ms`, `per_token_kernel_ms`, `cache_hit_rate`, `effective_batch_size`. Add per-route histogram for token_index vs latency and a kernel-version tag.

maya: Agree. Also add calibration metadata to traces: quant_mode, calibration_profile_id, scale_stats (min/max). That will help correlate quality vs perf.

olga: Quick config snippet for per-route observability (patch suggestion):
```yaml
route_metrics:
  enabled: true
  counters:
    - kernel_choice
    - pack_overhead_ms
    - memcpy_ms
    - kv_cache_hit
  histograms:
    - token_latency_by_index
  tags:
    - quant_mode
    - calibration_id
```

henri: Can we run an AB: fp8 with packing optimized (fast pack kernel) + relaxed admission vs current fp8 canary? Compare p99 and token histograms. If pack kernel reduces pack_overhead_ms from 0.12 to ~0.02 we should get parity.

sam: I'll spin an experiment: (A) fp8 current, (B) fp8 + fast_pack + relaxed admission, (C) int8 baseline. I'll keep prefix_cache on for all to reduce cache noise.

deploy-bot: Canary created: route=/canary/fp8-pack-test id=canary-20270415-11, variants=A,B,C. Traffic split 20/40/40.

maya: Thanks. One more ask: add kernel selection debug logs for a sample of requests (1/1000) to capture layer-level selection decisions — helps see fallback reasons.

olga: Will add that. Also pushing a perf regression alert rule: if memcopy fraction > 8% and p99 increases >5% vs baseline -> page oncall. For now it's investigational. :thinking_face: 

sam: Good. I'll post results in this thread once the AB finishes (give it ~2h). Thanks all. :eyes:
